title: Nine Months in a Tin
subtitle: 饼干与点心 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饼干与点心（生活与学习·饮食与烹饪）
meta: 主题语境：饼干与点心（生活与学习·饮食与烹饪）　|　核心词汇：biscuit　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 biscuit 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my grandmother was offered ① a biscuit that had been kept for nine months, and she said the offering was the whole of the visit. The ② biscuit, meaning the thing on the plate and not the kindness, was dry and was eaten anyway in eleven seconds; a biscuit, she said, is the only food that is accepted out of politeness and judged afterwards.

Every ③ biscuit in that tin had been bought for somebody else, and the ④ biscuit at the bottom, meaning the one saved for the minister and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever refused. A biscuit, my mother said, is nine parts tin and one part an occasion good enough to open it; my grandmother said the tin is the part that lasts.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ biscuit was the whole of the china, meaning the unglazed ware and not the food. The ⑥ biscuit, meaning the fired clay and not any of that, is the only thing in a cupboard that everybody breaks and nobody replaces; a biscuit, he said, is either something you dunk or the only word that means both a cake and a kind of clay. She said the clay came first.

By 1963 the ⑦ biscuit had become a photograph in a magazine, and the magazine had become an argument about the recipe. The ⑧ biscuit of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in April, was nine months in a tin and eleven seconds of eating; a biscuit, she said, is either the thing at the bottom or the reason you know who is coming. He said the knowing never needed a tin.

The ⑨ biscuit I remember is the one at the bottom, which was refused in 1966 and is still described as excellent. A ⑩ biscuit, my mother said in 1968, is the only food that improves by being refused; every biscuit, she said, is a clay that has agreed to look like a cake. She said the clay was never the point.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 饼干（指盘子上那个东西，与善意相对）
C. 固定搭配：be offered a biscuit 被递上一块饼干
D. n. 饼干（指铁盒里每一块）
E. n. 饼干（指盒子底那块）
F. n. 素瓷；未上釉的陶器
G. n. 素瓷（抽象：那种烧过的陶土）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a biscuit that had been kept for nine months
The biscuit, meaning the thing on the plate and not the kindness
biscuit was the whole of the china
The biscuit, meaning the fired clay
the biscuit had become a photograph in a magazine
The biscuit of the whole thing
A biscuit, my mother said in 1968

answers.why: be offered a biscuit 意为“被递上一块饼干”，1948 年有人递给祖母一块已经放了九个月的饼干。
biscuit 意为“饼干”，指盘子上那个东西而不是善意，它是干的，还是在十一秒内被吃掉了。
biscuit 指铁盒里每一块饼干，那个铁盒里每一块都是为别人买的。
biscuit 指盒子底那块（留给牧师的那块），是唯一有人拒绝过的。
biscuit 意为“素瓷、未上釉的陶器”，指那批瓷器，父亲说 biscuit 就是那批瓷器的全部。
biscuit 为抽象用法，指那种烧过的陶土，是碗柜里人人都打碎、却没人补上的东西。
biscuit 意为“饼干”，到 1963 年这个 biscuit 成了杂志里的一张照片。
biscuit 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，祖母四月写道，整件事权衡下来是在铁盒里放的九个月和十一秒的吃。
biscuit 意为“饼干”，我记得的是盒子底那块，1966 年被拒绝，至今仍被说成极好。
biscuit 为抽象总称，母亲说饼干是唯一会因为被拒绝而变好的食物。
